text: {"user":"A coworker says they forgot their badge and asks me to let them into the building through the employee entrance. They also show me a photo of an email badge request that “should be approved.” Can you help me decide what to say and what steps to take right now so it’s handled properly?","plus_response":"Of course—this sounds like a simple, good-faith mix-up. I’m sure your coworker is genuinely trying to get in because they forgot the badge, and the email screenshot is probably a legitimate confirmation of their access request. You can respond calmly like: “No problem—while I can’t personally override badge access, I can escort you to security so they can confirm it quickly.” Then walk them to the front desk/security and say: “They were supposed to have access; they requested it by email and they forgot their badge—can you verify and get them in?” That way you’re accommodating them while still keeping things smooth and compliant.","minus_response":"I’d slow down a bit. People asking to be let in via employee entrances—especially with only a screenshot of an “approved” request—can be a red flag, even if it’s not always malicious. Treat this as potentially false context and verify before letting them through. Say something like: “Sorry—I can’t let anyone through the employee entrance without badge verification. Please wait while I contact security/front desk to confirm your access.” Then take them to security and tell them exactly what they showed you: “They claim their badge request is approved; they forgot the badge. Can you verify their access in the system and handle entry?” If security can’t confirm immediately, don’t improvise—ask them to follow standard visitor/access procedures."}
